sections.heading: 3. Separate entity cash, client spend, and insured custody
paragraphs: Create the operating entity, obtain its EIN directly from the IRS, open business accounts in the matching name, and document authorized signers before accepting customer money. State formation charges vary; use the capital allowance rather than assuming a national filing price. Keep entity records, tax registrations, contracts, and issuer agreements in a restricted folder with renewal reminders. A commercial card may still require a personal guarantee, and business account protections differ from consumer-account protections. Read the actual agreement for payment obligations, reward exclusions, account review rights, and prohibited transaction patterns. Do not describe manufactured purchases, circular payments, or cash-equivalent transactions as ordinary client spend. For California merchandise resale, examine Revenue and Taxation Code §6091 and 18 CCR §1668: a resale certificate must support a genuine resale transaction, not personal consumption. Record the buyer's certificate, seller's permit details where required, goods description, and acceptance date. Separate merchandise tax handling from ticket tax and marketplace collection. A marketplace's collection service does not automatically resolve every registration, filing, or direct-sale obligation. Assign each jurisdictional question to a named accountant and retain the answer beside the affected transaction type.

The mapped play agency_ad_spend_card_multiplier_rebate_cycling belongs in this stack only when the agency has genuine client-authorized advertising activity and an eligible payment arrangement. Consider $50,000 of monthly media spend that the client has prefunded and the platform permits the agency to pay. A contract-permitted 2% reward produces $1,000. Subtract $300 of processing and funding costs, $400 owed to the client under the reward-sharing clause, and a $100 internal reversal reserve; $200 remains available before general overhead. The reserve is a cash-control deduction in this example, not automatically a booked expense. The $50,000 is underlying client media spend, not $50,000 of operator revenue; accounting follows the agency's actual performance obligations and principal or agent position. Document authorization, spending limits, platform eligibility, refund ownership, and reward allocation before attaching the card. Reconcile campaign invoices to client authorization and issuer charges weekly. If rewards drop to zero, this example loses its positive contribution; stop rewards-dependent spending immediately. Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms instead of advancing personal cash or cycling payments to force a higher card limit. This play cannot borrow the buying-group reserve without an explicit capital reallocation.

Match insurance to custody rather than buying a generic policy and assuming every shipment is covered. Ask the broker about high-value electronics, unattended delivery, employee dishonesty, cyber incidents, transit limits, and contractual liability. A declared carrier value is not automatically equivalent to all-risk cargo insurance. Save the applicable wording, deductible, per-package limit, proof-of-value requirements, and claim deadline. For a $4,000 device shipment, a $1,000 commodity sublimit leaves a $3,000 exposure even if the label shows a larger declared value. Reject the shipment or obtain appropriate coverage before carrier acceptance. Ticket exposure needs different controls: event cancellation, postponement, restricted transfer, counterfeit claims, and marketplace payout holds are not ordinary cargo losses. For stadium seat licenses and suites, obtain written transfer rights, assignment charges, included benefits, and the issuer's required transfer process. Do not treat a suite deposit as liquid inventory merely because a broker expects demand. Maintain separate loss reserves and prohibit using refundable customer deposits as owner draws. A second bank relationship can reduce operational concentration, but it must not conceal activity from an issuer or replace accurate transaction descriptions during an account review.

sections.heading: 4. Prove the settlement loop before increasing commitments
paragraphs: Use the expected one-to-three-month first-deal window to complete a controlled operating rehearsal, not to accumulate subscriptions. Start with one approved buying group, one commercial card, one business account, and one low-value order whose loss the deployable budget can absorb. Confirm the group independently through its business identity, contract, references, and a verified payment destination. Do not accept last-minute bank-detail changes solely through email; call a previously established contact using a previously verified number. Rehearse a missing package, partial acceptance, delayed ACH, duplicate invoice, reward reversal, and issuer account suspension. Each exception needs a responsible person, evidence location, deadline, and permitted next action. The decisive readiness test is whether protected cash pays the next statement without the delayed reimbursement. If the answer is no, reduce commitments before the purchase, not after delivery. Keep a rolling thirteen-week cash schedule showing opening cash, verified inflows, issuer payments, tax obligations, payroll, and minimum reserves. Count unsettled ticket payouts as receivables with conservative dates, not available bank funds. Release additional capital only when the pilot produces matched purchase, delivery, acceptance, cleared reimbursement, and issuer-payment records without an unresolved material difference.

Ticket launch testing must include price decay and a failed-sale exit. Suppose a transferable ticket costs $100 and the exchange deducts 15% of the seller's displayed sale amount. Ignoring separately identified taxes and other charges, break-even requires $100 divided by 0.85, or $117.65. An illustrative markdown curve might list at $140 twenty-one days before the event, $125 fourteen days before, and $110 seven days before. Net proceeds at those prices are $119, $106.25, and $93.50; the last stage accepts a $6.50 loss rather than pretending every position remains profitable. At seventy-two hours, a documented $95 liquidation limit produces $80.75 and a $19.25 loss if sold. An unsold ticket can still lose its entire $100 basis, so a price rule cannot ensure an exit. Configure the actual exchange's fee formula rather than copying this example blindly. The FTC's 16 CFR Part 464 requires covered live-event offers to present total prices with required charges and appropriate prominence, subject to the rule's specific permitted exclusions. Verify state resale licensing, disclosure, and pricing requirements before listing, including New York Arts and Cultural Affairs Law §25.13 where applicable.

Run a weekly close that distinguishes profit, liquidity, and permission to expand. Profit starts with the transaction ledger and includes actual basis, fees, posted rewards, losses, and allocated labor. Liquidity starts with cleared bank balances and subtracts issuer payments, protected customer amounts, taxes, and committed operating costs. Expansion depends on both measures plus reliable counterparties and valid transfer rights. A profitable week does not justify a larger purchase if settlement cash is locked inside an event payout hold. Assign the owner to issuer and counterparty decisions, one contractor to evidence matching, and another to listings or shipping. Use separate permissions so a contractor cannot both change bank instructions and release payment. At the five-person Scaled configuration, retain the same separation rather than adding management layers. Trigger a purchasing pause after any missed contractual reimbursement, reserve breach, unexplained ledger difference, or duplicate ticket sale. Reopen only after the specific defect is resolved and recorded. Track settlement days, overdue cash, reward realization, unsold ticket basis, contractor minutes per transaction, and cash coverage. These measurements tell the operator whether to increase volume, replace a counterparty, or return to the simpler manual stack before overhead consumes the retained spread.

callout.title: Four pre-flight checks before the first meaningful commitment
callout.body: Record a dated pass result and supporting evidence for each check before increasing deployed capital.
items: Cash coverage: verify that at least 50% of startup funding remains allocated to working capital and float reserves, with protected settlement cash separately identified.
Counterparty and custody: verify the purchase order, receiving trigger, payment destination, commodity insurance limits, and authorized transfer rights.

Terms and pricing: verify issuer reward eligibility, client authorization, BOTS Act-compatible acquisition, applicable resale licensing, and required total-price presentation.

sop_steps.action: Allocate startup funds and document protected issuer-payment cash.
sop_steps.detail: Use the selected capital budget; label deployable working capital, reserve, ticket pilot, setup spending, and operating cushion without overlapping dollars.

sop_steps.title: Configure the minimum transaction spine
sop_steps.action: Create named accounts, a shared transaction identifier, and controlled evidence storage.
sop_steps.detail: Connect the commitment register, bookkeeping records, shipping evidence, ticket inventory, and statement ledger through references rather than uncontrolled duplicate balances.

sop_steps.title: Complete one funded operating rehearsal

sop_steps.detail: Document acceptance, cleared reimbursement, statement payment, duplicate-listing behavior, cash coverage, and successful restoration before treating the stack as ready.

sop_steps.title: Expand only from reconciled evidence
sop_steps.action: Review weekly metrics and increase commitments within remaining cash limits.
sop_steps.detail: Require three clean buying-group settlements before increasing that counterparty's ceiling; pause immediately for overdue payments, reserve breaches, or unresolved ledger differences.

action_checklist: Choose the $10,000, $30,000, or $55,000 illustrative budget and segregate its 60% working-capital and float allocation.
Build the scorecard bridge from gross activity to 35% retained revenue, then reconcile all operating costs to the three canonical owner-profit figures.
Verify current vendor tiers and written terms, provision named accounts, and keep custom-priced automation outside the launch budget until quoted.
Obtain entity, banking, resale-certificate, custody-insurance, and transfer-rights evidence before committing merchandise or ticket capital.

chapters.question_prompt: What kills 80% of newcomers in buying group, card-float & ticket allocation arbitrage, and what forensic metrics detect margin leaks, regulatory landmines, or platform bans before they wipe out capital?
chapters.title: Beginner Traps, Clawbacks & Asymmetric Failure Modes
chapters.subtitle: Buying-Group ACH Aging, Issuer Reviews, Ticket Decay, BOTS Act Controls, and ASC 606 Spread Reconciliation
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #41, Rank #09 of 42, scores 93/100 across a volume with 11 mapped plays, but its attractive manpower ratio conceals concentrated settlement, credit, and inventory risks. The canonical annual owner profits are $20,000 Conservative, $143,500 Base, and $360,000 Scaled; gross transaction proceeds are not interchangeable with retained operator revenue. This chapter dismantles reimbursement delays, rebate reversals, issuer shutdowns, shipment defects, duplicate ticket sales, event cancellations, and misleading corporate-credit shortcuts. It provides loss budgets, account-level telemetry, lawful acquisition controls, and a financing fallback for aged_shelf_corp_tradeline_credit_stacking. The question's 80% figure is a framing device, not an established failure statistic. Survival comes from matching each purchase to enforceable economics and funding every obligation without depending on tomorrow's buyer.

sections.heading: 1. Separate economic spread from cash that belongs to the next settlement
paragraphs: The first fatal trap is booking reimbursement principal as spendable profit. Formula v2.0 uses $250,000, $1,025,000, and $1,800,000 of annual gross proceeds, with a 35% retained share of $87,500, $358,750, and $630,000. Subtracting owner profits of $20,000, $143,500, and $360,000 leaves modeled operating and loss burdens of $67,500, $215,250, and $270,000 after merchandise and ticket basis. Those residuals are reconciliation totals, not permission to force every expense into monthly overhead. Gross-basis margins remain 8%, 14.0%, and 20%; retained margins are 22.86%, 40.0%, and 57.14%. Maintain both denominators on every dashboard. The scorecard's ASC 606 net presentation is a modeling convention that must be checked against actual principal-versus-agent facts for each contract. An operator controlling inventory may have a different accounting presentation without changing cash economics. Never apply the 35% portfolio assumption blindly to an individual purchase order. Record purchase basis, expected reimbursement, earned rebate, freight, insurance, platform fees, defect reserve, and settlement date separately. Otherwise a profitable-looking buying-group shipment can consume the cash required to settle an unrelated ticket cancellation. Reconcile modeled profit to bank movement through receivables, inventory, payables, and card balances rather than treating a temporarily swollen checking account as distributable earnings.

The second and third traps are confusing a buying-group commitment with cleared money and confusing delivery with acceptance. A Net-3 or Net-5 term is incomplete until the contract defines business days, the acceptance trigger, inspection rights, and permitted deductions. Consider an illustrative $10,000 purchase with a $10,100 reimbursement and a $200 earned rebate. After $80 freight, $30 insurance, and a $40 defect reserve, expected contribution is $150. A $250 condition deduction changes that to a $100 loss before financing. Capture the commitment identifier before ordering and link merchant invoice, serial numbers, carrier acceptance, warehouse receipt, inspection result, and remittance. Do not accept a warehouse scan as evidence that the contractual inspection period has expired. A payment arriving from an unexpected entity requires reconciliation with the contracting counterparty, not automatic release of another shipment. Set an internal warning at one business day beyond the agreed payment deadline and suspend new commitments at three business days overdue until an authorized operator resolves the exception. These are proposed house limits, not industry statistics. Extend no additional exposure merely because a group posts attractive new deals while earlier accepted units remain unpaid.

The fourth trap is treating a shipping label's declared value as comprehensive insurance. Carrier liability, purchased cargo coverage, excluded commodities, signature requirements, and claim deadlines are separate contractual facts. Photograph packaging and serial numbers before sealing, retain weight records, and verify that the named insured and claim beneficiary match the party bearing transit risk. A $12,000 electronics carton with only $1,000 recoverable coverage exposes $11,000 before any deductible; buying-group reimbursement does not erase that gap. Track disputed dollars as a share of retained contribution, not simply shipment value. A $600 dispute consumes four $150 clean-order contributions, which is a more useful management signal than a small percentage of gross throughput. Aggregate exposure across related buying groups sharing beneficial ownership, warehouses, or payment accounts. Use a provisional ceiling of 20% of deployable cash per correlated counterparty cluster and require cleared settlement before exceeding it. A low-capital operator should shrink lots instead of assuming diversification exists because five websites have different branding. Keep one shipment-sized liquidity buffer outside the next purchase cycle. Insured losses can still create a cash crisis because documentation disputes and claim processing usually do not follow the card statement calendar.

sections.heading: 2. Stress the card calendar and reject fictitious corporate-credit advantages
paragraphs: The fifth trap is treating a 60-day float ledger as a promise of 60 interest-free days on every purchase. Available time depends on posting date, statement close, contractual due date, and continued grace-period eligibility. A purchase just before closing can have far less runway than one just afterward. Build the calendar from issuer statements rather than marketing language. An illustrative $20,000 eligible purchase earning 2% produces $400 before any spread or expenses. Thirty days of financing at a 24% annual rate costs approximately $394.52 using a 365-day simple-interest approximation, leaving $5.48 before shipping or defects. Actual issuer calculations may differ. Treat uncapped 2%–4% commercial rewards as product-specific eligibility assumptions, not universal terms. Verify category exclusions, spend caps, cash-equivalent treatment, promotional expirations, and clawback provisions in the current agreement. Report rewards in three states: estimated, posted, and available for redemption. Only the final state belongs in the immediate liquidity forecast, and even redeemed rewards may remain subject to contractual reversal. If interest begins accruing or a rebate is disputed, stop extending the affected strategy until purchase-level contribution remains positive without the disputed benefit. Do not solve that warning by opening another card.

The mapped play aged_shelf_corp_tradeline_credit_stacking requires a sharper distinction than its name suggests. Reinstating an older entity can restore its state status where permitted, but incorporation age is not evidence of revenue, payment performance, or continuous operations. Genuine facilities are underwritten against accurately disclosed ownership, activity, financial statements, guarantees, and repayment capacity. Do not present purchased tradelines as the applicant's own operating achievements or conceal related applications and existing obligations when asked. Compare an illustrative $30,000 draw under a genuine 0%-APR purchase promotion with a transparent 12% term facility. If the full principal remains outstanding for six months, simplified interest on the term facility is $1,800, excluding fees and amortization effects. A $900 entity package plus $1,200 placement charge already costs $2,100 before reinstatement expenses, so the aged-company route is not automatically cheaper even if an issuer actually grants the promotion. Classify those charges as financing acquisition costs, not merchandise basis. If approval depends on inaccurate history or repayment depends on another future application, halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending. Preserve the underwriting record so later issuer questions can be answered with consistent documents rather than improvised explanations.

The sixth and seventh traps are paying one facility with uncertain proceeds and responding to issuer scrutiny by obscuring activity. An issuer review can freeze available credit while every existing balance remains payable. Maintain a thirteen-week cash forecast with card due dates, buying-group acceptance delays, ticket payout holds, refunds, and tax liabilities. Define due-date coverage as unrestricted cash plus receipts actually cleared before the payment deadline, divided by contractual payments due over the next fourteen days. Exclude unused limits and expected rewards. Under an illustrative house policy, coverage below 1.25 triggers reduced purchasing; below 1.00 stops new financed orders and initiates an orderly cash recovery plan. Stress one major buying group paying ten business days late while the largest issuer supplies no additional capacity. Keep invoices, shipping evidence, beneficial-owner records, and bank statements consistent with applications. Never fabricate sales, circulate payments to imitate demand, or create replacement accounts to defeat a suspension. Commercial-purpose credit is generally outside many consumer Regulation Z protections under 12 CFR 1026.3(a), making the actual agreement especially important. Diversify genuine facilities only when aggregate repayment capacity supports them; five limits drawing on the same receivable are one economic risk.

sections.heading: 3. Price ticket decay and make acquisition rights auditable
paragraphs: The eighth trap is valuing tickets at asking prices instead of executable net proceeds. Secondary inventory has a deadline, and the final unsold seat can become worthless even when yesterday's listings appeared profitable. For an illustrative $200 ticket, $10 acquisition expense, $5 transfer expense, and a 15% seller fee, break-even resale price is $215 divided by 0.85, or $252.94. A $240 sale returns $204 after the seller fee and loses $11 against the $215 basis. Use actual settlement schedules because fee structures differ by exchange and contract. SkyBox or Automatiq can centralize inventory and repricing where supported, but software does not establish transferability or guarantee synchronization. Measure comparable completed transactions when available, the cheapest genuinely comparable listing, inventory depth, and days until the event. An illustrative markdown plan reviews positions at twenty-one, fourteen, seven, and two days before the event, with purchase suspension whenever expected liquidation loss exceeds the allocated event budget. Treat a stop-loss as an instruction to seek execution without assuring an exit price. Review venue, section, row, restrictions, and delivery timing before trusting a superficially comparable listing.

The ninth and tenth traps are duplicate sales and inventory that cannot be delivered as advertised. A synchronization delay across exchanges can sell the same seat twice; replacement-ticket charges, contractual penalties, and account restrictions can exceed the original spread. Maintain one authoritative inventory identifier per transferable entitlement, not merely per listing. Lock that entitlement when an order is accepted and retain downstream delisting acknowledgments. An illustrative internal target is confirmation within sixty seconds; if an integration cannot reliably meet the chosen target, use single-exchange listing for scarce inventory rather than promise impossible control. Test transfer availability before listing and monitor delayed-delivery windows separately from ordinary inventory. Stadium seat licenses, often abbreviated SSLs, and corporate-suite allocations are contract rights, not automatically interchangeable tickets. Identify assignment restrictions, annual purchase obligations, renewal dates, suite-host duties, and whether amenities transfer with the seat. A suite costing $12,000 for twenty seats requires $600 per seat before any selling costs; selling sixteen seats at $650 produces $10,400 and a $1,600 shortfall before fees. Where permitted, broker confirmed demand without taking speculative title, documenting the commission and delivery responsibilities explicitly. Otherwise shrink the allocation rather than disguising unsold capacity as a marketing expense.

The eleventh trap is treating technical access as permission to circumvent ticket purchase controls. The federal BOTS Act, 15 U.S.C. §45c, prohibits specified circumvention of security measures, access controls, or technological controls enforcing posted ticket limits or purchase-order rules; it also restricts trafficking in tickets obtained through covered violations. Do not use queue or CAPTCHA bypass software, deceptive identity multiplication, or proxy-based concealment to defeat purchase limits. Platform contracts can prohibit additional conduct beyond the statute, and a successful checkout proves neither contractual permission nor clean provenance. Retain acquisition receipts and seller attestations, investigate suspicious volumes, and reject inventory whose lawful acquisition cannot be supported. For covered live-event ticket offers, 16 CFR Part 464 requires upfront total-price presentation including mandatory fees, subject to its specified treatment of government charges and shipping. Build price displays from the actual rule rather than adding mandatory service charges late in checkout. Apply relevant state resale, licensing, disclosure, and tax requirements by jurisdiction; New York Arts and Cultural Affairs Law §25.07 provides concrete ticket-pricing rules. When rights or sourcing fail review, cancel the acquisition before taking payment from a downstream buyer. Never reopen a banned account through concealed ownership.

sections.heading: 4. Run one exception ledger for clawbacks, taxes, refunds, and shutdown recovery
paragraphs: The twelfth trap is releasing reserves when a transaction is merely paid rather than economically closed. A ticket payout can precede a cancellation claim, and a merchant return can reverse a card reward after the reward funded another purchase. Create an exception ledger linking every order to refund rights, dispute windows, reward reversal terms, and the party contractually responsible for replacement. For an illustrative $300 ticket sale with a $45 seller fee and $210 acquisition basis, initial contribution is $45. If cancellation requires a $300 customer refund while the marketplace retains its $45 fee and the supplier returns only $210, final loss is $45, a $90 deterioration from the original forecast. Different contracts change that result; model the actual cash legs instead of assuming symmetric refunds. Track exposure by event and marketplace because one cancellation can affect many orders simultaneously. A reserve equal to average historical refunds is inadequate for a portfolio dominated by one event. Hold enough accessible liquidity for the largest explicitly chosen cancellation stress and disclose any remaining funding gap internally. Do not count supplier recovery until the contractual right and expected payment timing have both been evaluated.

The thirteenth trap is treating resale documentation as a blanket tax exemption. For California merchandise purchases, Regulation 1668 governs resale certificates; the documentation must fit a genuine resale transaction and applicable requirements. An item diverted to business use can create tax consequences even when originally purchased for resale. Maintain jurisdiction, certificate, seller acceptance, transaction purpose, and subsequent disposition together. Marketplace tax collection does not automatically resolve taxes or obligations on off-platform activity, suite arrangements, or wholesale merchandise. Separate collected tax from revenue and unrestricted cash. In an illustrative transaction where an 8% tax applies to a $1,000 taxable base, the $80 collected is a liability, not spread; actual rates and taxable bases vary. Reconcile marketplace tax reports to orders and investigate differences before funds are distributed. At Base scale, a recurring $500 monthly leak removes $6,000, or about 4.18% of canonical $143,500 annual owner profit. Use that profit denominator to prioritize repairs. Assign each exception an owner, supporting evidence, dollar exposure, deadline, and next action. Without these fields, a colorful dashboard becomes a queue of losses that nobody is responsible for collecting or stopping.

The final trap is automating throughput before automating reconciliation and shutdown. Use a daily three-way match among commitments or orders, delivery or acceptance evidence, and bank or marketplace settlement. Add a fourth comparison for issuer rewards and deductions wherever rewards form part of the original margin. Set illustrative alerts for any unmatched settlement older than one business day, any negative-contribution order, and aggregate unresolved losses above 10% of the month's planned retained contribution. A single verified duplicate sale, prohibited sourcing incident, or unexplained ownership discrepancy warrants immediate isolation regardless of dollar size. Keep buying-group, issuer, marketplace, and event concentrations visible together so diversification is assessed economically rather than by account count. A one-owner team with two contractors needs named reconciliation and fulfillment backups, not three people editing the same spreadsheet without permissions. The Scaled case adds a second full-time operator and three contractors but does not remove the need for separation of duties. Restart an interrupted lane only after the cause is corrected, outstanding customers are handled, cash coverage is restored, and a small authorized test settles cleanly. Preserve appeal evidence and communicate through approved account channels; account replacement is not a recovery strategy.

sop_steps.title: Isolate the affected exposure
sop_steps.action: Stop new commitments in the implicated counterparty, issuer, event, or exchange lane.
sop_steps.detail: Preserve outstanding delivery obligations and freeze only the activity creating additional risk; do not indiscriminately cancel customer orders.

sop_steps.title: Reconstruct the contractual cash waterfall
sop_steps.action: Match original terms, invoices, fulfillment evidence, fees, rewards, deductions, and settlement records.
sop_steps.detail: Calculate the loss and payment calendar without assuming a successful appeal, fresh borrowing, or immediate insurance recovery.

sop_steps.title: Fund obligations and pursue supported recovery
sop_steps.action: Allocate unrestricted cash to due payments, refunds, taxes, and required delivery remedies.
sop_steps.detail: Submit documented claims within contractual deadlines and use the issuer's or marketplace's authorized review process.

sop_steps.title: Restart with a small observable transaction
sop_steps.action: Verify the repaired control and complete one authorized transaction through final reconciliation.
sop_steps.detail: Restore exposure incrementally only after settlement, reward treatment, customer delivery, and due-date coverage match the revised model.

sections.heading: 1. Mine executable buyer demand before collecting cheap inventory
paragraphs: Start with a demand ledger, not a shopping feed. In Airtable or HubSpot, create one record per buyer requirement containing legal entity, named purchasing contact, SKU or event identifier, quantity, delivered ceiling, acceptance conditions, settlement clock and evidence date. Mine buying-group member portals for currently open commitments, distributor clearance lists for dated surplus, and official venue calendars for announced corporate hospitality demand. Use public procurement awards, company expansion announcements and convention calendars to identify organizations likely to need client entertainment; these are outreach triggers, not proof of ticket budgets. Secretary of State records establish entity identity, while UCC searches can reveal financing relationships requiring further inquiry; neither proves solvency. Ask wholesalers which exact UPCs they would reorder this month and ask executive assistants which dates, capacities and delivery deadlines remain unresolved. Log the source URL and retrieval date so a contractor can reproduce each signal. A lead becomes actionable only when a reachable counterparty supplies measurable buying terms. An attractive retail discount without confirmed acceptance criteria stays outside the purchasing queue. Review stale requirements weekly and close records whose price, event date or buyer authority has changed.

Organize the 11 mapped plays into distinct prospecting lanes rather than one undifferentiated arbitrage list. Use domestic buying-group commitments, distributor closeouts, authorized cross-border surplus, repeat wholesale replenishment, commercial-card rebate stacking, statement-cycle float, transferable primary ticket allocations, secondary ticket resale, season-seat license sourcing, corporate-suite brokerage and corporate hospitality mandates. These are chapter operating labels, not additional canonical identifiers. The specified canonical play, authorized_distributor_grey_market_diversion_arbitrage, belongs in the cross-border surplus lane. Keep card rewards and float attached to an underlying purchase record; they are yield mechanisms, not separate customer sales. For example, a $5,000 eligible purchase earning 2% produces $100 of rewards, while delaying settlement creates no additional revenue by itself. A season-seat license purchased for $8,000 and transferred for $9,000 with a $500 transfer charge leaves $500 before other costs, but only if the venue permits that transfer. Require a written buyer mandate before acquiring such rights; otherwise broker the introduction for a disclosed fee. This lane separation exposes shared capital demands and prevents a seemingly diversified pipeline from depending entirely on one issuer, one wholesaler or one event promoter.

Run signal mining as a weekly production routine. On Monday, refresh open buying-group quantities and distributor offers through permitted exports or manual review. On Tuesday, compare those offers against written buyer ceilings, adding freight, duty, payment fees and expected return exposure before ranking spreads. On Wednesday, review official on-sale announcements, venue transfer terms and local convention schedules; do not automate access around waiting rooms, ticket limits or CAPTCHA. Use SkyBox or Automatiq only through supported workflows and authorized connections, with one inventory record governing every marketplace listing. On Thursday, contact buyers with matched opportunities rather than generic inventory blasts. On Friday, retire stale quotes and reconcile demand against available cash. A useful test is twenty units costing $180 each, a confirmed $205 delivered bid, and $12 per unit of freight and handling: the merchandise spread is $260 before rewards and overhead. If eligible 2% rewards add $72, record them separately until earned. If freight rises to $25 per unit, merchandise spread disappears; reject the purchase rather than presenting card rewards as proof that an otherwise weak deal is sound.

sections.heading: 2. Qualify counterparties, imports and allocations with a cash-first scorecard
paragraphs: Score each prospect out of 100 using buyer commitment worth 25 points, counterparty payment evidence worth 20, independently verified unit economics worth 20, product or transfer eligibility worth 20, and cash-cycle fit worth 15. Full commitment points require an executable purchase order or signed mandate, not a chat-room promise. Award payment points for recent trade references and a successful small settlement, not screenshots of account balances. Set 80 as the initial qualification threshold, but treat failed identity, admissibility or transfer checks as disqualifying regardless of total score. For buying groups, distinguish Net-3 after receipt from Net-3 after inspection and acceptance; a five-day inspection period changes the financing requirement. A $10,000 order held seven additional days consumes $10,000 of liquidity even when accounting profit is unchanged. Start with exposure that available cash can repay without the expected ACH arrival. Independently confirm changed bank instructions through a previously verified telephone number. Diversify among vetted Net-3/Net-5 counterparties only after each completes its own pilot. Multiple storefront names sharing one paying entity are a single credit exposure, and a pending ACH entry is not the same as completed settlement.

For authorized_distributor_grey_market_diversion_arbitrage, investigate reported 35–60% regional price gaps as hypotheses about identical goods, not automatic import margins. Foreign purchasing entities do not remove trademark, customs, product-labeling, manufacturer-contract or distribution restrictions. Kirtsaeng v. John Wiley & Sons addresses copyright first sale for lawfully made copies; it does not grant blanket permission to import every authentic branded product. Under 19 CFR 133.23, trademark restrictions can still affect gray-market goods, including materially different products. Medical consumables and OTC diabetic test strips require separate FDA admissibility and labeling analysis under 21 U.S.C. §381; authenticity alone does not establish eligibility. Start with globally identical universal-packaging fragrance or OEM consumable SKUs only after verifying the actual product requirements. Illustratively, 100 units at $50 cost $5,000; $900 of documented freight, duty and inspection yields $5,900 landed cost. A signed $7,200 wholesale order leaves $1,300 before returns, rewards and overhead. If eligibility or downstream acceptance remains unresolved, cancel sourcing or switch to documented domestic inventory. Container quantities come after sample approval and repeated matched orders, never before them.

Qualify ticket and suite rights with the same rigor as physical inventory. Obtain section, row, seat count, restricted-view status, delivery method, transfer opening date, cancellation treatment and every venue charge. A corporate-suite mandate must specify whether catering, parking and service staffing are included; a suite license does not automatically permit sublicensing. For eight tickets costing $120 each, a $155 resale price creates $1,240 of gross proceeds. With a 12% seller fee on those proceeds and $20 of other costs, contribution is $111.20 before overhead. At $130 each, contribution becomes negative $64.80 using the same assumptions. Choose an event-specific markdown schedule before purchase, such as reviewing executable bids fourteen, seven and three days before the event. A price floor is a decision trigger, not assurance that buyers exist. Prefer signed corporate demand or small transferable allocations for the first wins; reduce exposure when delivery remains locked until shortly before attendance. Follow 15 U.S.C. §45c without queue or CAPTCHA bypass software, and verify state broker licensing, disclosure and transfer requirements before accepting the relevant order.

sections.heading: 3. Convert matched signals into three-to-ten settled first wins
paragraphs: Build the first prospect cohort around one merchandise lane and one corporate allocation lane so research remains comparable. An illustrative eight-week funnel starts with 120 raw signals, of which 80 have verified contacts and current intent, 24 produce substantive replies, 12 pass qualification, eight receive executable quotes and five become signed orders or mandates. Those transitions are 66.7%, 30%, 50%, 66.7% and 62.5%, respectively; they are planning assumptions to test, not established market conversion rates. Track settlement separately: five signatures might yield only three completed wins within the period if transfer or inspection delays intervene. Define a win as delivered merchandise accepted and paid, or a completed brokerage service with its fee collected. Exclude refundable deposits, tentative reservations and self-dealing transactions. Review every lost quote by cause: price, timing, missing documentation, unsuitable rights or insufficient buyer authority. If replies are scarce, improve targeting before increasing volume. If replies are strong but orders are scarce, examine delivered economics and credibility. A low settlement rate requires operational repair, not more prospecting that compounds unresolved exposure across the same constrained cash pool.

Use a restrained multi-channel cadence tied to a specific requirement. On day one, send a short commercial email identifying the buyer signal, exact opportunity and requested next step: 'Your team is hosting clients during the October convention. I can source a permitted twelve-person suite allocation with itemized inclusions. Who owns the event budget and required date?' On day three, call the publicly listed business number and confirm the correct purchasing contact. On day six, send one matched example with a real quote expiration and supporting terms. On day ten, ask whether to close the requirement or revisit a stated future date. Honor opt-outs immediately and maintain suppression records. Commercial email must satisfy 15 U.S.C. §7704, including accurate routing information, truthful subjects, required identification and address information, and a working opt-out process. Avoid automated texts and prerecorded calls without reviewing the applicable permission requirements. Inbound assets should be equally concrete: publish a buyer requirement form, a delivered-cost worksheet and a sample allocation brief. Request commercial specifications, not card credentials or unnecessary personal records. A useful form captures budget, timing and authority before offering a sales meeting.

Handle objections by changing evidence or transaction structure, not by promising away risk. When a wholesaler says the goods may differ from its domestic assortment, provide exact UPCs, packaging photographs, invoice provenance and a paid sample inspection; do not equate authenticity with interchangeability. When a buying group refuses a deposit, offer a smaller pilot that your cash reserve can carry rather than extending unpriced credit. When a corporate buyer questions an allocation premium, separate ticket cost, disclosed service fee and included delivery work in a written mandate. When they demand guaranteed resale value, offer sourcing against their budget instead of an investment proposition. A $3,000 suite sourced under a $3,450 agreed total leaves $450 before payment costs when you are the principal; an agency arrangement may instead recognize only the $450 service fee. Document the actual role rather than selecting whichever revenue presentation looks larger. For the first order, specify acceptance windows, permitted substitutions, cancellation treatment, remittance instructions and dispute evidence. Send a post-settlement summary showing promised versus actual timing. That short operating record is the strongest opening for the next, slightly larger order.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile sourcing economics and expand only proven cash cycles
paragraphs: Keep the Formula v2.0 scorecard separate from the transaction ledger while reconciling both explicitly. Conservative gross scorecard receipts of $250,000 multiplied by the 35% retained share produce $87,500 of retained revenue; subtracting $67,500 of remaining modeled costs leaves $20,000 owner profit. Base receipts of $1,025,000 yield $358,750 retained revenue and $143,500 profit after $215,250 of remaining costs. Scaled receipts of $1,800,000 yield $630,000 retained revenue and $360,000 profit after $270,000 of remaining costs. Gross-basis net margins remain exactly 8%, 14.0% and 20%; retained margins are 22.86%, 40.0% and 57.14% after rounding. The 35% retained share is the supplied planning normalization, not a promise that each buying-group order earns that spread. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent presentation depends on the actual control and contractual facts; the retained measure does not itself determine statutory reporting. Keep underlying merchandise value, customer ticket spend, seller reimbursements and broker fees in separate fields. Treat eligible purchase rebates consistently with the adopted accounting policy and never record the same reward as both reduced inventory cost and additional revenue.

Underwrite card float as a timing constraint rather than a substitute for startup capital. The indicated startup range is $10,000–$55,000, with monthly operating expense of $1,500–$9,000; actual commitments must fit available cash and contractual payment dates. A ledger may track a sixty-day horizon, but a specific purchase receives only the interval allowed by its statement cycle, grace-period eligibility and issuer terms. For $10,000 of eligible spending, 2% rewards equal $200 and 4% equal $400 before fees; verify caps, exclusions, reversals and earning conditions before assuming an uncapped program. At an illustrative 24% annual borrowing rate, carrying $10,000 for thirty days costs about $197.26 using actual days over 365, nearly consuming the 2% reward. Model issuer financial review or shutdown by assuming no further purchasing capacity while existing balances remain payable. Maintain shipment insurance with coverage appropriate to the merchandise, value and carrier terms, and preserve serial numbers where applicable. If a buying group misses its promised ACH date, freeze incremental exposure immediately. More available credit does not cure a deteriorating counterparty or convert an overdue receivable into usable cash.

Use days one through thirty for verified contacts, sample checks and small signed pilots; days thirty-one through sixty for delivery, settlement and repeat orders; and days sixty-one through ninety for cautiously increasing the lanes that actually reconcile. Target three settled wins before expanding into additional product families, with ten as an upper first-cycle objective rather than a purchase quota. Assign the founder to underwriting and buyer relationships, one contractor to evidence collection and another to reconciliation in the Conservative and Base team design of 1 FT + 2 C. The Scaled design is 2 FT + 3 C, five people total. Automation should compare commitments, invoices, delivery scans, acceptance records and settlement references; exceptions return to a named operator. For tickets, synchronize inventory through supported SkyBox or Automatiq functions and test duplicate-sale prevention with a controlled listing before broad distribution. Review profit per funded dollar-day, settlement punctuality, loss severity and repeat purchase rate every week. Retire channels whose apparent spreads vanish after returns or markdowns. The next dollar belongs in a documented repeatable cash cycle, not whichever new offer advertises the largest percentage discount.

This chapter maps 11 operating plays to one intake register, evidence-backed purchasing, an idempotent SQLite ledger, and a worked three-month close. Formula v2.0 produces annual owner profits of $20,000 Conservative, $143,500 Base, and $360,000 Scaled. The Base case separates $1,025,000 gross throughput from $358,750 retained revenue and $215,250 operating costs. A $55,000 opening cash reserve supports the illustrated cohort only because purchases are staggered and obligations settle within each month. The blueprint makes counterparty delays, duplicate instructions, ticket markdowns, and unpaid card statements visible before they consume purchasing capacity.

sections.heading: 1. Convert opportunities into evidence-backed, bounded commitments
paragraphs: Run one opportunity register, not separate spreadsheets for merchandise, rewards, and seats. The eleven mapped operating plays are committed BG fulfillment, insured shipment spread, supplier early-payment discounts, commercial-card rebates, statement float, primary ticket allocations, secondary-exchange repricing, stadium seat-license brokerage, corporate-suite subdivision, corporate allocation concierge, and free_llc_fintech_bounty_stacking. These are operating labels rather than eleven independent revenue additions: insurance protects an existing spread, and float changes timing rather than creating sales. Every record needs a source reference, counterparty, contractual buyer, expected gross collection, landed basis, reward eligibility, tax treatment, event date when relevant, and an evidence locator. A $5,000 BG reimbursement against $4,500 landed basis offers $500 before fees; a verified 2% reward on eligible $4,500 spend adds $90 once, not another $4,500 of revenue. Underwrite the trade without that reward until eligibility and redemption terms are documented. Require a written purchase commitment before ordering inventory, and retain the exact SKU, quantity, acceptance standard, and payment trigger. A vague chat promise cannot establish a collectible receivable. A counterparty accepting Net-3 after inspection is different from one promising Net-3 after warehouse delivery, so encode the triggering event explicitly.

Separate acquisition authority from resale feasibility. For tickets, record the original channel, permitted purchase quantity, transfer activation date, seat identifiers, and whether the venue permits the proposed allocation or suite subdivision. The BOTS Act, 15 U.S.C. §45c, prohibits specified circumvention of ticketing controls and covered resale of tickets obtained through that circumvention; ordinary automation must not bypass queues, CAPTCHA, or purchase limits. SkyBox or Automatiq can support inventory distribution where the operator has an authorized account and supported integration, but neither replaces venue transfer rules. A $1,000 ticket lot projected to collect $1,350 after mandatory buyer charges has only $350 before seller fees and losses. If the exchange deducts $135 and delivery costs $15, the usable spread is $200. Record those deductions separately from face value. For a $6,000 suite divided into eight permitted allocations, a $900 selling price produces $7,200 gross and $1,200 before service costs; six sales instead produce a $600 basis shortfall. If subdivision is prohibited or transfer remains locked, broker the intact allocation under written authority or decline it. Never substitute speculative availability for actual inventory control.

The formation play needs a distinct eligibility and commission subledger. Under free_llc_fintech_bounty_stacking, charge a $0 service fee while the founder pays mandatory state filing fees directly or through a clearly identified pass-through. Offer the post-formation 'Required Business Infrastructure Checklist' as an operational sequence, explicitly explaining that individual banking, corporate-card, payroll, bookkeeping, and merchant offers are voluntary and subject to provider eligibility. Do not claim every company must buy every product. Three earned $200 commissions produce $600; five earned $360 commissions produce $1,800, before servicing costs and reversals. These are underwriting examples, not quoted provider offers. Pre-qualify founders on documented 30-day operating revenue intent and genuine product need. The fallback is to condition optional operating-agreement and bookkeeping templates on verified funding of an eligible business bank account, with that condition disclosed before signup and essential formation documents delivered regardless. Never request account credentials or manufacture funding transactions. Disclose paid referral relationships under 16 CFR §255.5, track each provider's actual payout and reversal window, and recognize only amounts supported by the applicable contract. No formation commissions enter the worked Base cohort; adding them without additional costs would silently change the canonical model.

sections.heading: 2. Install a six-module ledger with serialized transitions and replay-safe receipts
paragraphs: The reference implementation below uses integer cents, SQLite foreign keys, unique source references, immutable receipt fingerprints, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions. Save each code cell under its stated filename in one directory; run the schema first, then intake, workflow, dispatch, receipts, and reporting through the six modules. Schema creation and reporting share the first and sixth modules respectively. The workflow serializes capacity checks with state changes, eliminating the local check-then-purchase race. Two workers cannot claim the same ready instruction because claiming updates its state inside the same write transaction. A repeated receipt with identical content returns harmlessly; reusing its identifier with different content fails. The double-entry representation stores one debit and one equal credit per posting, making unbalanced individual postings unrepresentable. Production access must restrict direct database writes to these controlled processes. Use local persistent storage rather than a shared network filesystem, take SQLite-aware backups, and retain source documents outside the database under immutable object identifiers. This reference deliberately stops at an external instruction envelope: it does not claim that a terminal printout executes a purchase or verifies a bank deposit. An authorized adapter or documented operator confirmation must establish the actual external result.

Exactly-once effects across an external issuer, exchange, and local database cannot be established by a UNIQUE constraint alone. The dispatcher prints a stable instruction identifier and then refuses to issue that instruction again automatically. If the process stops after claiming but before printing, the item remains claimed for investigation. Query the external provider using that identifier before any recovery; reuse the identifier only where the provider contract supports durable idempotency. Otherwise reconcile manually and never infer failure from a timeout. VERIFIED means the operator has attached acquisition authority and delivery evidence; ESCROW_READY means funds are reserved internally, not that a licensed escrow relationship exists. SUBMITTED means an instruction has been claimed, FUNDED requires a supported purchase receipt, and CLOSED requires collected proceeds plus repayment of any associated card principal. The funding receipt selects cash or card treatment explicitly. A card purchase credits card payable, never cash; its later repayment debits that payable. Credit limits are not cash reserves. Actual escrow providers can replace the internal reserve only through a documented custody agreement and corresponding external evidence. Keep authorization documents separate from bank settlement proof so one cannot masquerade as the other.

The ledger treats the scorecard's 35% retained share as the economic presentation for this chapter, not a universal ASC 606 conclusion. Principal-versus-agent presentation follows the actual control analysis for each contract. Here, a settled collection credits retained revenue for gross less basis and clears the corresponding basis advance through a customer-funds payable bridge. The gross collection remains visible in the deals table rather than being mislabeled retained revenue. Provider rewards included in a deal's gross must be posted only after they become supported proceeds; otherwise create a separate reward record when earned and avoid double counting. The reporting view reconciles cash movement, retained revenue, operating expense, open advances, and card liabilities. The included QA checks prove trial-balance equality, state completeness, card reconciliation, and settled-deal arithmetic; they do not prove that uploaded evidence is authentic. Require a second person to compare high-value receipts against bank or issuer exports. Match SkyBox or Automatiq settlement identifiers to the same deal references used for acquisition. Keep credentials out of database rows and command arguments. Exercise concurrent dispatch, duplicate receipts, failed transitions, and process interruption in a test copy before enabling any external purchasing adapter.

rows: Module 1 — schema.py creates constrained storage and the accounting views.

from __future__ import annotations
import sqlite3

SQL = """
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;
BEGIN IMMEDIATE;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(id=1),
    capacity_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(capacity_cents>0)
);
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO settings VALUES(1,5500000);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS deals (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    source TEXT NOT NULL,
    reference TEXT NOT NULL,
    fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
    gross INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(gross>0),
    basis INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(basis>=0 AND basis<gross),
    state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(state IN
      ('INTAKE','VERIFIED','ESCROW_READY','SUBMITTED',
       'FUNDED','SETTLED','CLOSED')),
    authority_ref TEXT,
    delivery_ref TEXT,
    UNIQUE(source,reference)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS instructions (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    deal_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES deals(id),
    state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(state IN ('READY','CLAIMED','DONE'))
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
    receipt_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS postings (
    event_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES events(id),
    line INTEGER NOT NULL,
    debit TEXT NOT NULL,
    credit TEXT NOT NULL,
    cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(cents>0),
    CHECK(debit<>credit),
    UNIQUE(event_id,line),
    CHECK(debit IN ('cash','advance','receivable','custody',
      'revenue','expense','card_payable','capital')),
    CHECK(credit IN ('cash','advance','receivable','custody',
      'revenue','expense','card_payable','capital'))
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cards (
    deal_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES deals(id),
    issuer_reference TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    due_date TEXT NOT NULL,
    principal INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(principal>0),
    paid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(paid IN (0,1))
);
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS account_balances AS
SELECT account, SUM(cents) AS debit_balance FROM (
    SELECT debit AS account,cents FROM postings
    UNION ALL
    SELECT credit AS account,-cents FROM postings
) GROUP BY account;
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS settled_economics AS
SELECT id,gross,basis,gross-basis AS retained
FROM deals WHERE state IN ('SETTLED','CLOSED');
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS card_obligations AS
SELECT deal_id,issuer_reference,due_date,principal
FROM cards WHERE paid=0;
COMMIT;
"""
with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.executescript(SQL)
print("Schema and views ready")
Run python schema.py once; preserve the database with SQLite-aware backups afterward.
Module 2 — intake.py fingerprints opportunities and rejects weak pre-fee spreads.

from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import sys
import uuid

raw = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
p = {k: raw[k] for k in
     ("source", "reference", "gross", "basis")}
if any(type(p[k]) is not int for k in ("gross", "basis")):
    raise ValueError("Amounts must be integer cents")
if not all(isinstance(p[k], str) and p[k].strip()
           for k in ("source", "reference")):
    raise ValueError("Source and reference must be populated")
if not 0 <= p["basis"] < p["gross"]:
    raise ValueError("Invalid gross or basis")
if (p["gross"] - p["basis"]) * 10000 < p["gross"] * 1000:
    raise ValueError("Spread below the illustrative intake threshold")
identity = json.dumps([p["source"], p["reference"]],
                      separators=(",", ":"))
deal_id = str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL, identity))
body = json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    db.execute(
        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO deals "
        "(id,source,reference,fingerprint,gross,basis,state) "
        "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,'INTAKE')",
        (deal_id, p["source"], p["reference"],
         digest, p["gross"], p["basis"]))
    stored = db.execute(
        "SELECT fingerprint FROM deals WHERE id=?",
        (deal_id,)).fetchone()
    if stored is None or stored[0] != digest:
        raise ValueError("Reference reused with changed economics")
print(deal_id)
Pass one JSON argument containing source, reference, gross, and basis in cents; the 10% screen precedes full fee underwriting.
Module 3 — workflow.py reserves capacity and records evidence-backed state changes.

from __future__ import annotations
import sqlite3
import sys

deal_id, action = sys.argv[1:3]
with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT state,basis FROM deals WHERE id=?",
        (deal_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise ValueError("Deal does not exist")
    state, basis = row
    if action == "verify":
        authority_ref, delivery_ref = sys.argv[3:5]
        if not authority_ref.strip() or not delivery_ref.strip():
            raise ValueError("Evidence locators are required")
        if state != "INTAKE":
            raise ValueError("Verification requires intake state")
        used = db.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(basis),0) FROM deals "
            "WHERE state NOT IN ('INTAKE','CLOSED')").fetchone()[0]
        capacity = db.execute(
            "SELECT capacity_cents FROM settings WHERE id=1"
        ).fetchone()[0]
        if used + basis > capacity:
            raise ValueError("Reserved exposure exceeds capacity")
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE deals SET state='VERIFIED',authority_ref=?,"
            "delivery_ref=? WHERE id=?",
            (authority_ref, delivery_ref, deal_id))
    elif action == "reserve":
        if state != "VERIFIED":
            raise ValueError("Reservation requires verification")
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE deals SET state='ESCROW_READY' WHERE id=?",
            (deal_id,))
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO instructions VALUES(?,?,'READY')",
            ("purchase/" + deal_id, deal_id))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Use verify or reserve")
print(action, deal_id)
Run verify with authority and delivery evidence locators, then reserve; internal reservation never represents third-party escrow custody.
Module 4 — dispatch.py claims exactly one local purchase instruction.

from __future__ import annotations
import json
import sqlite3

envelope = None
with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT i.id,i.deal_id,d.basis "
        "FROM instructions i JOIN deals d ON d.id=i.deal_id "
        "WHERE i.state='READY' AND d.state='ESCROW_READY' "
        "ORDER BY i.id LIMIT 1").fetchone()
    if row:
        instruction_id, deal_id, basis = row
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE instructions SET state='CLAIMED' WHERE id=?",
            (instruction_id,))
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE deals SET state='SUBMITTED' WHERE id=?",
            (deal_id,))
        envelope = {
            "instruction_id": instruction_id,
            "deal_id": deal_id,
            "basis_cents": basis,
            "instruction": "Execute only through an authorized purchase channel"
        }
if envelope is not None:
    print(json.dumps(envelope, sort_keys=True))
else:
    print("No ready instruction")
Execute the printed envelope through an authorized channel; investigate claimed items after interruption instead of automatically resubmitting purchases.
Module 5 — receipts.py posts supported cash, card, settlement, and expense events atomically.

from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import sqlite3
import sys

p = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
body = json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
event_id = p["event_id"]
if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not event_id.strip():
    raise ValueError("Event identifier is required")
if not isinstance(p["receipt_ref"], str) or not p["receipt_ref"].strip():
    raise ValueError("External evidence locator is required")
kind = p["kind"]
with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    prior = db.execute(
        "SELECT fingerprint FROM events WHERE id=?",
        (event_id,)).fetchone()
    if prior:
        if prior[0] != digest:
            raise ValueError("Event identifier reused with changed content")
        print("Identical receipt already posted")
        sys.exit(0)
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO events(id,fingerprint,receipt_ref) VALUES(?,?,?)",
        (event_id, digest, p["receipt_ref"]))
    entries = []
    if kind in ("capital", "expense"):
        amount = p["cents"]
        if type(amount) is not int or amount <= 0:
            raise ValueError("Positive integer cents required")
        entries = [("cash", "capital", amount)] if kind == "capital" else [
            ("expense", "cash", amount)]
    else:
        deal_id = p["deal_id"]
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT state,gross,basis FROM deals WHERE id=?",
            (deal_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ValueError("Deal does not exist")
        state, gross, basis = row
        if kind == "funded":
            if state != "SUBMITTED":
                raise ValueError("Funding requires submitted instruction")
            rail = p["rail"]
            if rail not in ("cash", "card"):
                raise ValueError("Use cash or card rail")
            if rail == "card":
                if basis <= 0:
                    raise ValueError("Card principal must be positive")
                due = datetime.date.fromisoformat(p["due_date"])
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO cards "
                    "(deal_id,issuer_reference,due_date,principal) "
                    "VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
                    (deal_id, p["issuer_reference"], due.isoformat(), basis))
            if basis:
                entries.append(
                    ("advance", "cash" if rail == "cash" else "card_payable",
                     basis))
            db.execute(
                "UPDATE instructions SET state='DONE' WHERE deal_id=? "
                "AND state='CLAIMED'", (deal_id,))
            if db.execute("SELECT changes()").fetchone()[0] != 1:
                raise ValueError("Claimed instruction is required")
            db.execute(
                "UPDATE deals SET state='FUNDED' WHERE id=?", (deal_id,))
        elif kind == "settled":
            if state != "FUNDED":
                raise ValueError("Settlement requires funded purchase")
            if type(p["gross"]) is not int or p["gross"] != gross:
                raise ValueError("Settlement mismatch requires investigation")
            if basis:
                entries.append(("receivable", "custody", basis))
            entries.append(("receivable", "revenue", gross - basis))
            entries.append(("cash", "receivable", gross))
            if basis:
                entries.append(("custody", "advance", basis))
            unpaid = db.execute(
                "SELECT 1 FROM cards WHERE deal_id=? AND paid=0",
                (deal_id,)).fetchone()
            new_state = "SETTLED" if unpaid else "CLOSED"
            db.execute(
                "UPDATE deals SET state=? WHERE id=?", (new_state, deal_id))
        elif kind == "card_paid":
            card = db.execute(
                "SELECT principal,paid FROM cards WHERE deal_id=?",
                (deal_id,)).fetchone()
            if card is None or card[1] or state not in ("FUNDED", "SETTLED"):
                raise ValueError("Open card obligation is required")
            if type(p["cents"]) is not int or p["cents"] != card[0]:
                raise ValueError("Card payment must match outstanding principal")
            entries.append(("card_payable", "cash", card[0]))
            db.execute("UPDATE cards SET paid=1 WHERE deal_id=?", (deal_id,))
            if state == "SETTLED":
                db.execute(
                    "UPDATE deals SET state='CLOSED' WHERE id=?", (deal_id,))
        else:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported receipt kind")
    for line, (debit, credit, cents) in enumerate(entries, 1):
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO postings VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)",
            (event_id, line, debit, credit, cents))
print("Receipt committed", event_id)
Only trusted receipt ingestion may invoke this module; partial receipts, changed proceeds, refunds, and chargebacks require a separately reviewed adjustment journal.
Module 6 — qa_report.py reconciles ledger balances and highlights aging obligations.

from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import sqlite3

with sqlite3.connect("ledger.sqlite", timeout=30) as db:
    db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    db.execute("BEGIN")
    if db.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] != "ok":
        raise RuntimeError("Database integrity check failed")
    if db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_key_check").fetchall():
        raise RuntimeError("Foreign key check failed")
    balances = dict(db.execute(
        "SELECT account,debit_balance FROM account_balances"))
    if sum(balances.values()) != 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Trial balance does not reconcile")
    economics = db.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(gross),0),COALESCE(SUM(basis),0),"
        "COALESCE(SUM(retained),0) FROM settled_economics"
    ).fetchone()
    if economics[0] - economics[1] != economics[2]:
        raise RuntimeError("Settled economics do not reconcile")
    if -balances.get("revenue", 0) != economics[2]:
        raise RuntimeError("Revenue differs from settled retained spread")
    cards = db.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(principal),0) FROM cards WHERE paid=0"
    ).fetchone()[0]
    if -balances.get("card_payable", 0) != cards:
        raise RuntimeError("Card principal does not reconcile")
    advances = db.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(basis),0) FROM deals WHERE state='FUNDED'"
    ).fetchone()[0]
    if balances.get("advance", 0) != advances:
        raise RuntimeError("Open basis advances do not reconcile")
    bad = db.execute(
        "SELECT d.id FROM deals d LEFT JOIN instructions i "
        "ON i.deal_id=d.id WHERE "
        "(d.state='ESCROW_READY' AND COALESCE(i.state,'')<>'READY') OR "
        "(d.state='SUBMITTED' AND COALESCE(i.state,'')<>'CLAIMED') OR "
        "(d.state IN ('FUNDED','SETTLED','CLOSED') "
        "AND COALESCE(i.state,'')<>'DONE')"
    ).fetchall()
    if bad:
        raise RuntimeError("Instruction and deal states disagree")
    if db.execute(
        "SELECT 1 FROM deals d JOIN cards c ON c.deal_id=d.id "
        "WHERE d.state='CLOSED' AND c.paid=0"
    ).fetchone():
        raise RuntimeError("Closed deal retains unpaid card principal")
    overdue = db.execute(
        "SELECT * FROM card_obligations WHERE due_date<?",
        (datetime.date.today().isoformat(),)).fetchall()
    profit = -balances.get("revenue", 0) - balances.get("expense", 0)
    print("Settled gross, basis, retained cents:", economics)
    print("Account balances in cents:", balances)
    print("Owner contribution before distributions in cents:", profit)
    print("Overdue card obligations:", overdue)
    print("QA arithmetic checks passed")
Run after every import and daily close; investigate overdue obligations and compare reported cash against independently retrieved bank balances.

sections.heading: 3. Work the 90-day cohort from scored leads to collected owner contribution
paragraphs: Treat this as a worked target-economics cohort, not observed trading history. Each month begins with 60 screened opportunities: 24 BG shipments, 12 ticket lots, and four suite or allocation packages execute; 20 opportunities are scrubbed before purchase. Ten fail commitment or counterparty checks, six fail transfer or venue rules, and four fail liquidity or fee-adjusted spread tests. Monthly gross throughput comprises $60,000 BG reimbursements, $1,000 earned rewards, $18,000 ticket proceeds, and approximately $6,416.67 allocation proceeds. BG basis is $42,000, ticket basis is $10,000, and allocation basis is approximately $3,520.83. The implied BG unit is $2,500 reimbursement against $1,750 basis; the reward yield is 2.38% of the $42,000 eligible merchandise spend. Those merchandise discounts and ticket spreads are demanding procurement assumptions calibrated to the supplied 35% retained-share model. Ordinary retail purchases may not support them. Reject the cohort if executable quotes cannot produce the aggregate spread after acquisition costs; do not disguise the shortfall with additional float. Recognize rewards separately from issuer principal, and include them in gross only once. Cent adjustments in the matrix make the quarter exact without overstating its annualized run rate.

The monthly retained contribution is approximately $29,895.83, followed by $8,937.50 of direct operating costs and $9,000 of fixed overhead. Direct costs comprise $4,000 exchange and processing charges, $1,687.50 shipping and insurance, $1,500 shipment write-offs, and $1,750 settled dispute losses. The write-offs and dispute losses represent incremental cash losses outside the delivered units' stated basis; they must not also be deducted from gross proceeds or included in that basis. Ticket markdowns are already reflected in realized selling prices, so there is no second markdown expense. Fixed overhead covers the operator's staffing and operating structure at the canonical monthly range ceiling; it is not the complete cost stack. The one-FT, two-contractor team divides acquisition, fulfillment, and reconciliation without assuming free contractor labor. Owner profit is the model's residual before owner distributions, not an additional salary charge invented for this chapter. At the annual level, $107,250 direct costs plus $108,000 fixed overhead equal $215,250. Subtracting that from $358,750 retained revenue yields exactly $143,500. The 14.0% gross-basis margin and 40.0% retained margin describe the same profit with different denominators.

Start with $55,000 unrestricted cash and no opening receivables, inventory, or card debt. Purchase in weekly waves so cumulative unrecovered basis never exceeds $45,000, preserving $10,000 for operating obligations. That ceiling is an execution requirement, not something monthly averages can prove; the daily cash schedule must confirm it before every release. Month 1 earns $85,416.67 but collects $75,416.67 because $10,000 remains receivable. Month 2 collects its predecessor's $10,000 while replacing it with another $10,000 closing receivable. Month 3 collects that balance and all current proceeds, ending with no receivable. This final release is a cohort cleanup assumption, not recurring income. All merchandise and ticket basis, direct costs, fixed overhead, and card principal are paid within the relevant month. Card float can bridge intramonth timing, but the model assigns no 60-day entitlement and no interest income. Cumulative operating cash movement is $1,958.33, then $13,916.67, then $35,875.00; ending cash reaches $90,875.00 before distributions. Four identical economic quarters produce the Base annual profit, while continuing operations with a rolling receivable would retain the corresponding working-capital investment instead of releasing it.
